questions.question: What should be done with a disabled bus that has passengers still on board?

options.text: Do not push it with another bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not push it with another bus.
questions.explanation: A disabled bus with passengers should not be pushed or towed by another vehicle. The only exception is if it is unsafe for passengers to exit where the bus stopped. In that case, the bus may be towed or pushed to a safe location.

questions.question: What should the driver do after students get off the bus at school?

options.text: Assume all students took their belongings.
Assume the doorway is clear right away.
Walk through the bus to check for any students who are sleeping or hiding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus to check for any students who are sleeping or hiding.
questions.explanation: After all students exit, the driver should walk through the bus to look for any students still on board who may be hiding or sleeping. The driver should also look for items students may have left behind.

questions.question: During a school bus evacuation, which exit should passengers use?
questions.correctAnswerText: The safest exit available.
questions.explanation: During an emergency evacuation, the driver must quickly decide which exit is safest and direct all students to use that exit.

questions.question: How many classes of hazardous materials are there?
questions.correctAnswerText: Nine
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are divided into nine classes. Each class describes a different type of risk.

questions.question: During a bus evacuation, students must be led at least ____ away from the road.
questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: Students must be led at least 100 feet away from the road. The driver should lead them toward oncoming traffic. This distance protects them from flying debris if another vehicle hits the bus.

questions.question: When is an outside convex mirror properly adjusted?

options.text: When the driver can see at least one lane of traffic and the entire side of the bus.
When the driver can see the front bumper.
When the driver can see the top of the bus.
When the driver can see the front windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the driver can see at least one lane of traffic and the entire side of the bus.
questions.explanation: The mirrors should show the fronts of the rear tires on the ground, each side of the bus to the mirror, and at least one traffic lane on both sides of the bus.

questions.question: What should a bus driver do when arriving at a destination?

options.text: Wait to announce until the bus has stopped and passengers are getting off.
Remind passengers to take their belongings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remind passengers to take their belongings.
questions.explanation: The driver should remind passengers to take their belongings before leaving the bus. This announcement is best made before the bus comes to a complete stop.

questions.question: How far away from students should a bus driver stop at a bus stop?
questions.correctAnswerText: At least 10 feet
questions.explanation: The bus should stop at least 10 feet away from students. This makes students walk toward the bus, so the driver can watch their movements and know where they are.

questions.question: What must bus drivers do at railroad crossings?

options.text: They do not need to stop.
They do not need to stop but must slow to 25 mph below the speed limit.
They do not need to stop but must open the door to listen for trains.
They must stop and check for approaching trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must stop and check for approaching trains.
questions.explanation: Bus drivers must stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail track to look and listen for trains. Only proceed when certain no trains are coming. You do not need to stop at streetcar crossings, when a police officer or flagger is directing traffic, at green traffic signals, or at crossings marked "exempt" or "abandoned."

questions.question: What do outside crossover mirrors help a driver see?

options.text: The right side of the bus
The left side of the bus

questions.correctAnswerText: The front bumper
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors help the driver see the danger zone in front of the bus and on the left and right sides. They show the area from the front of the bus to the service door.

questions.question: Buses should never transport:
questions.correctAnswerText: Radioactive materials.
questions.explanation: Buses cannot carry labeled radioactive materials where passengers sit. Small arms ammunition labeled ORM-D, emergency hospital supplies, and medicines are allowed.

questions.question: A bus driver's seat must have:

options.text: A storage pocket on the left side.
A storage pocket on the right side.

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat belt.
questions.explanation: The driver's seat must have a seat belt. The driver should always wear it.

questions.question: Before driving a bus that has been parked for several days, you should:

options.text: Walk through the bus to check for any damage since the last trip.
Ask passengers to check the inside of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus to check for any damage since the last trip.
questions.explanation: Unattended buses can be damaged. Before driving, check the inside to make sure everything is in good condition.

questions.question: Carry-on luggage should be:

options.text: Stored so the driver can move freely and passengers can exit safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stored so the driver can move freely and passengers can exit safely.
questions.explanation: All baggage must be stored so the driver can move freely, passengers can exit from any door or window in an emergency, and items cannot fall or shift and hurt riders.

questions.question: If your bus's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) fails:

options.text: You will have no brakes at all.
The brakes will work slower than normal.
You will still have normal braking power.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will still have normal braking power.
questions.explanation: If the ABS is not working, the bus will still have regular braking power. Continue to drive and brake normally.

questions.question: To prevent passenger problems with safety and behavior rules, you should:

options.text: Not seat passengers next to each other.
Explain the rules at the start of the trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain the rules at the start of the trip.
questions.explanation: Many carriers have rules about smoking, drinking, and music on buses. Explaining these rules at the beginning of a trip helps prevent problems later.

questions.question: An emergency roof hatch:

options.text: Must be locked closed before driving.
Can be partially open while driving to let in fresh air.
Should only be opened in an emergency.
Should always be open while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be partially open while driving to let in fresh air.
questions.explanation: Emergency roof hatches can be locked in partially-open positions for fresh air. Do not leave them open as a regular practice. An open hatch increases the bus's clearance height.

questions.question: You should sign a previous driver's vehicle inspection report if:

options.text: The previous driver dated their entry.
Any reported defects have been fixed.
You will drive more than one hour or 50 miles.
The report is on the dashboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any reported defects have been fixed.
questions.explanation: Sign a previous inspection report only if defects were fixed or if no repairs were needed.

questions.question: The emergency exit door:

options.text: Can be opened if the bus gets too hot while driving.
Can be opened while driving if the bus is carrying cargo.
Can be opened while backing for a better view.
Should never be open while the bus is driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be open while the bus is driving.
questions.explanation: Check all emergency exits before driving. Never drive with an emergency exit door or window open.

questions.question: When should you check the bus mirrors?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before driving the bus.
questions.explanation: Check the mirrors before each trip. Adjust them as needed before you start driving.
